description.narrative:
This project will devise, develop and establish a mode of delivery for a learning series that has learning outcomes relevant to the whole organisation and is pitched at appropriate levels for a wide range of learners. The series will focus on race, racism, racialisation and decoloniality and the relationships between these and poverty. Objective: 1. To determine the common understanding of ‘decolonisation’ and anti-racism for an average Nigerian 2. What impact does decolonisation have to ending poverty and shifting power in Nigeria 3. What is the connection between colonialism, poverty and development practice in Nigeria and internationally?
Objectives for Comms Plan: 1. To increase understanding on practices that promote decolonisation and anti-racism at work targeting development practitioners through targeted social media campaigns and a hybrid dissemination event by August 2024.
2. To increase awareness of and accessibility to evidence and learning resources produced by the research by August 2024. 1. A teaching and accompanying set of multi-media learning resources that CA can use to deepen understanding of decolonisation among its staff/partners and critically reflect on our programme approaches for development, advocacy and humanitarian work. 2. An online seminar organised by CA to present the Nigeria case study. 3. A final reading learning piece that can be published.
